subject: Measurement invariance for binary + continuous data

messages.author: 8c60e30b41bed636
messages.subject: Measurement invariance for binary + continuous data
parts:
Dear all,

I am trying to examine measurement invariance of a factor model that uses both binary and continuous data. I have not found an example of this kind of situation anywhere and I repeatedly encounter errors. Does anyone have any information about how to do this?

Also, I read that for testing measurement invariance of binary indicators one should directly test scalar invariance directly. Does this hold true when using mixed, binary and continuous, indicators?

Thank you very much
Irene

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance for binary + continuous data
parts:
I don't know of any such tutorials.  I would recommend you (1) manually (i.e., using labels in your syntax) constrain loadings to equality ONLY for continuous indicators first.  Compare that model to the configural model, to test metric invariance of continuous indicators.  (2)  Then you fit a model that additionally constrains loadings of binary indicators, as well as their thresholds, and the intercepts of continuous indicators.  That model lets you test scalar invariance of all indicators.

DIF in loadings cannot be distinguished from DIF in thresholds or intercepts for binary indicators, so you can only test scalar invariance of those indicators.
